source: Authenticated status SSE subscriptions, retained JSONL history, and live run events.
control: A bounded event broker enforces global, per-principal, and per-run subscriber quotas, bounded per-consumer queues, one-time replay, backpressure deadlines, sequence-gap failure, retention, and disconnect cleanup without polling storage.
sink: Control Center SSE response writers, Node.js event-loop capacity, and status-event storage reads.
boundary: Authenticated principals may open streams, but no principal or run may allocate unbounded subscribers, queued bytes, or repeated full-history parsing.

pre_fix_negative.result: Exact pre-fix polling and full-file replay functions amplified history reads across concurrent clients and ignored response backpressure.

tests.aggregate: Final control-services local suite: 120/120 passing; shell/script checks: 57/57 passing.

independent_qa.local_evidence: Deterministic regression and aggregate suites passed on the cohort branch.
independent_qa.required: Re-run after patch-equivalent cherry-pick and exercise concurrent SSE behavior under representative runtime load.

runtime_status.evidence: Local Node tests exercised broker, storage, response, abort, and backpressure fakes; no production listener or service was started.

external_conditions: Production reverse-proxy connection limits and representative concurrency/load evidence remain deployment-owned.

rollback.safety: Revert only with SSE disabled or an equivalent bounded stream control in place; otherwise the pre-fix amplification returns.

source: Append-only status-event JSONL files, including histories with large or malformed prefixes and records.
control: Reverse-tail reads enforce byte and record ceilings before parsing, reject an oversized selected record, and validate only the bounded suffix.
sink: One-shot status-event API responses and Control Center memory/CPU used to read and parse history.
boundary: An authorized caller may request recent events, but historical file size and attacker-shaped earlier records cannot force a full-file read.

pre_fix_negative.result: The exact pre-fix implementation read and parsed the full synthetic history before applying the requested result limit.

tests.aggregate: Final control-services local suite: 120/120 passing; shell/script checks: 57/57 passing.

independent_qa.local_evidence: Focused bounded-tail and aggregate suites passed on the cohort branch.
independent_qa.required: Re-run after patch-equivalent cherry-pick and profile a representative large production-format history.

runtime_status.evidence: Disposable local files were exercised; no Control Center service or production state file was opened.

external_conditions: Production retention sizing and filesystem latency remain deployment-owned observations.

rollback.safety: Revert only with the one-shot status endpoint disabled or an equivalent pre-parse tail bound in place.

source: Hosted project metadata selected through the verified workload pointer and lock.
control: Metadata is pre-bounded by file size and YAML shape budgets, parsed in an interruptible worker with a deadline, content-addressed by digest, and accepted only when that digest and path are bound to the verified workload lock.
sink: Project Router discovery, cache entries, and upstream routing decisions.
boundary: A hosted workload author may shape metadata, but cannot make routing consume unbounded input or substitute metadata outside the verified lock generation.

pre_fix_negative.result: Bounded synthetic oversized, deep, high-alias, and repeatedly changing files reached the exact pre-fix unbounded read/parse path.

tests.aggregate: Project Router focused suite: 6/6 passing. Final control-services local suite: 120/120 passing; shell/script checks: 57/57 passing.

independent_qa.local_evidence: Focused router and aggregate suites passed on the cohort branch.
independent_qa.required: Re-run after patch-equivalent cherry-pick and verify a prepared hosted lock generation through the assembled router runtime.

runtime_status.evidence: Worker deadlines, cache binding, and lock/pointer tampering were exercised with disposable fixtures; no live hosted workload or router listener was used.

external_conditions: Hosted deployment must prepare and atomically publish the verified workload lock and pointer with the expected private ownership and permissions.

rollback.safety: Revert support before the primary cohort commit, and disable hosted metadata routing unless equivalent parse budgets and verified-lock binding remain.

source: Read-only hosted project directory trees whose depth, width, file sizes, symlinks, and filesystem latency may be workload-shaped.
control: Disk accounting runs asynchronously with explicit depth, node, byte, time, and concurrency ceilings, does not follow symlinks, coalesces in-flight scans, yields to the event loop, and serves explicit stale last-known-good data when truncated.
sink: Control Center context construction, filesystem operations, and Node.js event-loop availability.
boundary: A hosted workload author may shape the mounted tree while an authenticated viewer triggers context construction; the scan must remain bounded and disclose truncated or stale state.

pre_fix_negative.result: The exact pre-fix synchronous walker exhausted disposable wide, deep, symlinked, and slow trees without depth, node, byte, or time ceilings.

tests.aggregate: Final control-services local suite: 120/120 passing; shell/script checks: 57/57 passing.

independent_qa.local_evidence: Focused scanner and aggregate suites passed on the cohort branch.
independent_qa.required: Re-run after patch-equivalent cherry-pick and measure representative mounted-filesystem latency and concurrent requests.

runtime_status.evidence: Disposable synthetic trees exercised the scanner; no mounted production project, HTTP listener, or container was used.

external_conditions: Production tree scale, mount latency, and acceptable stale-data thresholds require operational calibration.

rollback.safety: Revert only with project disk accounting disabled or replaced by another bounded asynchronous/precomputed source.

source: Requests to phpMyAdmin and phpPgAdmin routes carrying only the server-side Control Center session cookie plus proxy target metadata.
control: Dedicated-host native-login routes are removed; retained portal routes invoke fail-closed ForwardAuth first, trust no forwarded identity assertions, validate exact host/path/method targets, and require the existing fresh owner session authorization.
sink: Traefik routing to phpMyAdmin or phpPgAdmin and the Control Center internal database-admin authorization endpoint.
boundary: Private-network reachability, native database-admin login, viewer/admin roles, stale owner sessions, and spoofed headers are insufficient; only a fresh authenticated owner session may pass.

pre_fix_negative.result: Both dedicated database-admin routers reached native login without the fresh-owner middleware for anonymous, viewer, admin, and stale-owner cases.

independent_qa.local_evidence: Structural routing, target-gate, auth configuration, and aggregate tests passed on the cohort branch.

runtime_status.evidence: No Traefik, Control Center listener, OIDC provider, database UI, private network, or browser session was started.

external_conditions: Live OIDC session freshness, Traefik ForwardAuth transport, and portal host configuration require deployment evidence.

rollback.safety: Revert only with both database-admin services unreachable or an equivalent fresh-owner gate enforced before native login.
